name: Bouquet Green
lede: Bouquet Green is a soft teal-green that Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary dates to 1927, measured about ten units from the everyday name Jade.

sections.title: A 1927 entry, no story attached
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul's *A Dictionary of Color* (1930) places Bouquet Green on plate 27, position H7, and dates its first recorded use to 1927 [1]. The dictionary does not explain the name beyond the plate position, and no connection to a specific flower arrangement is documented here [1]. The ISCC-NBS 1955 lists do not carry the name separately, and the National Bureau of Standards circular cites only Maerz and Paul's entry [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[corsage-green]], [[verdigris-green]] and [[deep-malachite-green]], at 3.1, 3.2 and 3.8 ΔE [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
This is an uncommon painted color: our archive finds a match to this swatch in 26 of 23,781 paintings, 0.11 percent, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 8, rarer than 70 percent of the named colors we track [3]. The sample is too small to support a reliable painter or country figure, so none is claimed here [3].

The color peaks in the 1900s, four times the expected rate across 1,674 paintings from that decade, though the count behind that figure is only 5 paintings [3]. The earliest match dates to 1857, by Alexander von Kotzebue, 73 years before the name's 1930 record, which shows only that a similar-looking hue existed in paint before the word did, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3]. These are photographs of varnished paintings, read as screen colors [3].
